notes.decision: Translated 'the fourth Father.' ⲙⲁⲍ-ϩⲧⲁⲩ = ordinal 'fourth' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four'). The previous page presumably enumerated Fathers 1–3; this page begins with the fourth and reaches the fifth at line 12. The 'second' (line 6) and 'third' (line 9) inside this section refer to the three subsidiary ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'powers' called by the fourth Father.

Translated 'powers' rather than 'mights/strengths' (per accumulated vocab note). In this enumeration the three ⲛⲟⲁⲙ are clearly distinct cosmological agents (Apostle, Call, Form of Light) parallel to the standard Manichaean triad of emanations, where 'powers' is the conventional rendering for δυνάμεις.

Translated 'at the time to bear.' ⲡⲥⲁⲡ = 'the turn / the season / the appointed time.' ϩⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ = ⲣ̄- + Greek φορέω 'to bear/wear,' here used of the Apostle's incarnational bearing of the church-of-flesh.

Translated 'the Call' (capitalized). The technical Manichaean cosmological figure (Syriac qrīā, Greek κλῆσις) — the Call from the Father of Greatness which descends with the Apostle as his Twin/yokefellow. The following line's ⲛ̄ϣⲃⲣ̄ⲁⲟⲩⲏⲧ 'yokefellow' confirms this identification.

Translated 'yokefellow.' Compound ϣⲃⲏⲣ ('companion') + ⲟⲩⲏⲧ ('single, sole, joined'). Captures the unique-companion / united-partner sense — the Manichaean Twin/Syzygos who is bound to the apostle as one. 'Yokefellow' preserves the unitive bond.

Translated 'to attend him.' Verbal root ⲗⲁⲍⲧ̄ uncertain; possibly ⲗⲁϩⲥ̄ 'cleave/cling' or related to ⲗⲁϩⲙⲉϥ 'attendance.' Context (the Companion remaining beside the apostle in every place) supports a 'be near / attend / cling-to' sense.

Translated 'afflictions.' Greek loanword most likely θλίψις 'tribulation, affliction,' with Coptic spelling ⲑⲁⲓⲧⲓⲥ where -ⲗ- has been elided/assimilated. Paired here with κίνδυνοι 'dangers,' a standard Pauline-style doublet (Rom 8:35).

Translated 'the fifth Father also.' ⲙⲁⲍⲧⲟⲩ = ⲙⲁϩϯⲟⲩ 'fifth.' ⲍⲱϣ = ⲍⲱⲱϥ 'himself / also' (Lyc.). This Father differs from the fourth: where the fourth's Form of Light is received at renunciation (entry into the elect), the fifth's Form of Light is revealed at death (exit from the body).

Translated 'the one to hold.' ⲡⲟⲩⲉ = 'the one (of them),' introducing the first of the three angels. The series continues 'the second' (line 16) and 'the third' (line 17), each holding a different regalia.
Translated 'the prize.' Greek βραβεῖον — the victor's prize/award (Phil 3:14, 1 Cor 9:24). Standard Manichaean term for the eschatological reward presented to the soul at death.
Translated 'the diadem.' Likely the Coptic equivalent of διάδημα or a head-band/fillet, listed alongside ⲡⲥⲧⲉⲫⲁⲛⲟⲥ ('wreath') and ⲡⲕⲗⲁⲙ ('crown') as three distinct items of regalia.

Translated 'These are those of him who will recognize them.' Reading ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲁⲥⲛⲟⲩⲱⲛⲟⲩ as a form of ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲁⲥⲟⲩⲱⲛⲟⲩ 'who will know/recognize them' (with anomalous ⲥⲛ for ⲥⲟ). The cluster ⲛⲉⲓⲉⲧϩ̄ is morphologically obscure; tentatively parsed as ⲛⲉⲓ ⲉⲧ-ⲏ̄ⲡ '(those) who pertain to.'
Translated 'so that some (attain) life forever.' ⲭⲉ = 'so that, because.' ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ = ϣⲁ ⲉⲛⲉϩ 'forever, eternally.' The construction 'some of life forever' is elliptical; supplying 'attain' for sense.
Translated 'men of mercy.' ⲥⲁⲛ- (collective 'men of') + ⲣ̄- + ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϩⲣⲉ ('mercy, compassion'). Paired with 'the righteous of peace' as the two classes of recipients of the garments of light.

Translated 'mounts.' ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄-ⲧⲉⲗⲟ = 'place of mounting' = 'vehicle, mount, conveyance.' The kephalaion treats Jesus's modes of entry into the world as 'mounts' which he successively rides — preserving the verb-of-mounting (ⲧⲉⲗⲟ) imagery.
Translated 'the Man of Light.' ⲣⲙ̄-ⲛ̄-ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ = 'man of light.' Mani's self-designation as the speaker of the kephalaia. Distinct from ⲡⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ ('the Illuminator'); preserve the literal compound.

Translated 'the vessel of light.' ⲭⲁⲓ uncertain — possibly 'vessel, frame, ship-body' (cf. ϫⲁⲓ 'ship'). Given the chapter's vehicle/mount imagery, 'vessel' fits the conveyance semantics better than 'body' (which would be ⲥⲱⲙⲁ). Tentative.
